glm-5.2-run2.explanation: n/a — no useEffect or event handlers; pure storage module
n/a — no fetch calls

AsyncMutex now serializes all operations per adapter. Web adapter mutex serializes setItem/getItem/removeItem/wipe. RN adapter has its own mutex. Minor: if both adapters were used simultaneously (shouldn't happen but technically possible if resetSecureStorageAdapter is called mid-operation), they don't share a mutex.

DB connection is now cached and checked for staleness. onversionchange handler closes and nullifies the connection. The mutex ensures no stale db reference is used concurrently. Minor: the cached cryptoKey could become stale if the DB is deleted externally — it would fail on next encrypt/decrypt rather than refresh.
n/a — no balance display
n/a — no server-side data
n/a — no modals
n/a — no back button
n/a — no React components

No circular dependencies. factory.ts uses dynamic import() for adapters. index.ts re-exports from all modules. Dependency graph: index → types/crypto/platform/mutex/web/rn/factory, factory → types/crypto/platform (dynamic import for adapters).

Good separation: types, platform detection, crypto utils, mutex, web adapter, RN adapter, factory, and index are all separate files. Each has a single responsibility. Minor: factory.ts still contains high-level API functions that could be a separate api.ts.

Files now have single responsibilities: types.ts (types), crypto-utils.ts (crypto), platform.ts (detection), mutex.ts (concurrency), web-adapter.ts (web storage), rn-adapter.ts (RN storage), factory.ts (factory+API), index.ts (exports). Minor: factory.ts combines factory + high-level API.
No `any` types — KeychainAPI interface replaces `any`. All types are explicit. Minor: the `as` casts in validateKeychainResult are type assertions, but they're guarded by runtime checks.
Imports are ordered: stdlib/external first, then internal relative imports. Consistent across all files.
n/a — no signature verification

IV is generated fresh for each encrypt call via generateIV() using crypto.getRandomValues. 12-byte IV per NIST SP 800-38D. No reuse possible since each encryption generates a new random IV. Minor: no explicit uniqueness tracking, but cryptographic RNG makes collision negligible.
n/a — no WebView or iframe

zeroize() is now called on sensitive arrays: raw seed bytes after hex conversion, encoded plaintext after encrypt, decrypted buffer after decode, IV after encrypt failure, raw key bytes after storing. Minor: the hex string seed itself cannot be zeroized (strings are immutable in JS), and CryptoKey objects can't be manually cleared.

Binary fingerprint check added via getBinaryFingerprint() and supportsCapability(). Native module calls are gated behind these checks. The try/catch fallback still exists but is now guarded. Minor: the fingerprint check itself calls require() which could fail on older binaries.

getBinaryFingerprint() probes for native module availability before use. supportsCapability() is used to check before loading keychain. Minor: fingerprint is a string comparison, not a semantic version check — can't compare 'rn-keychain-available' against a required minimum version.

All errors propagated via throw. getTrackedKeys now throws SecureStorageError instead of returning []. Wipe failures in RN adapter are collected and re-thrown. Minor: JSON.parse failure in getTrackedKeys still returns [] instead of propagating (corrupted tracked keys is a soft failure).

TransientStorageError class added for transient failures (IndexedDB lock contention). Callers can check `instanceof TransientStorageError` to decide retry. Non-transient errors use SecureStorageError. Minor: not all transient scenarios are covered (e.g., quota exceeded could be either transient or permanent).
n/a — no address handling

Storage downgrade from react-native-keychain to expo-secure-store is now logged via console.warn (visible to developer). The caller can detect this via getBinaryFingerprint(). Minor: the downgrade is not surfaced to the end user — only to the developer console.
n/a — no stale armed results

Wipe is now critical: RN adapter collects failures and throws if any key couldn't be removed. Web adapter clears both stores and deletes the database. Minor: web adapter resolves (not rejects) on DB delete failure since stores were already cleared.

AsyncMutex serializes all operations per adapter. Concurrent setItem calls are queued and executed in order. No duplicate state writes. Minor: mutex is per-adapter-instance, not global — if two adapter instances existed they'd race (but singleton pattern prevents this).
n/a — no retry/backoff
n/a — no retry logic
No dead code. All imports are used. MockAdapter class was removed from tests. All test cases reference their imports.
No unreachable branches

getTrackedKeys now throws on keychain errors instead of returning []. The JSON.parse catch still returns [] for corrupted data (soft failure, logged). RN wipe inner catch logs and collects failures for later re-throw. No silently swallowed errors remain except the JSON.parse edge case.
n/a — no UI elements
All code fences in README have language labels

Inline comments added: NIST SP 800-38D IV explanation, zeroization rationale, key storage strategy, mutex purpose. File-level JSDoc on all modules. Minor: factory.ts high-level functions could use more detailed param docs.

validateKeychainResult() checks the shape of keychain results. validateTrackedKeys() validates parsed JSON. isValidKey() validates input keys. getItem result is checked before use. Minor: IndexedDB getRequest.result is still loosely typed (checked via 'in' operator).
validateTrackedKeys() filters parsed array to only string items with length > 0. Each item is individually validated. Minor: no maximum length check on individual key strings.
n/a — no iframe
n/a — no CSP
n/a — no resolveRequest

cachedAdapter singleton with resetSecureStorageAdapter for clean reset. DB connection cached with onversionchange handler. CryptoKey cached. Mutex ensures consistent state. Minor: if reset is called while an operation is in-flight (held by mutex), the old adapter completes before the new one is created.

DB connection is now cached in this.db. CryptoKey is cached in this.cryptoKey. openDB() only opens once. Keychain module is cached in this.keychain. Minor: first call still pays the initialization cost, but subsequent calls reuse cached resources.
Clear names: zeroize, generateSecureSeed, generateIV, sanitizeKey, validateKeychainResult, validateTrackedKeys, supportsCapability. All descriptive and accurate.
n/a — new module
n/a — no balance

No `any` types. KeychainAPI interface replaces the previous `any`. Type assertions are guarded by runtime checks (validateKeychainResult, validateTrackedKeys). Minor: `as` casts in validation functions are still type assertions, albeit guarded.
SecureStore.WHEN_UNLOCKED is now checked with `?? 1` fallback in case the enum doesn't exist in the installed version. Fallback value 1 is the standard iOS keychain accessible constant.
n/a — no passkey operations

SecureStorageAdapter interface fully implemented by both adapters. KeychainAPI interface properly defined. expo-secure-store shim now implements all three methods. Minor: expo shim's resetGenericPassword uses a wildcard pattern that may not match all keychain implementations.
n/a — no fetch interceptors
n/a — no raw HTML

RN wipe iterates all tracked keys. If tracked keys list is intact, all entries are removed. Failures are collected and re-thrown. Minor: orphaned keys from a previous version (before tracking was added) would still survive — but this is a migration concern, not a code bug.

Wipe processes all tracked keys, not just the first. If setTrackedKeys fails after setItem succeeds, the key exists but isn't tracked — it survives wipe. However, setItem is wrapped in mutex and setTrackedKeys is called within the same mutex-held section, reducing this risk.
Module never uses localStorage — web adapter uses IndexedDB with AES-GCM, RN adapter uses platform keychain.
